title: Orchestrated version attrition and migration journey for legacy model interfaces
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Safely retire legacy model interfaces and tags that are incompatible with the runtime-1.22 optimizations while providing a low-friction migration path for customers. This ticket coordinates cross-team tasks for launch planning, release notes, staged comms, and customer migration tooling.

Scope: legacy model tags older than v2024-10 that rely on the deprecated KV layout and pre-1.20 kernel assumptions. We will: 1) announce the attrition runway and migration timeline, 2) publish migration guides and SDK shims, 3) update runtime routing and default fallbacks, 4) deprecate tags after a minimum notice window, and 5) execute a phased removal with canary and gated stages.

Success criteria: migration guides published, SDK shim with automated compatibility layer released, >=85% of active customers on compatible tags or using shim before hard-deprecation window, release notes and GTM comms issued to customers and partner teams, and no P0 incidents attributable to the decommissioning during rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Public migration guide in Docs with step-by-step for API changes and sample prompts
SDK shim (node + py) published to npm/pypi and referenced in migration docs
Release notes entry ready and scheduled in release-automation with change-id
Support playbook and canned responses authored and reviewed
Canary group roll completed (10 customers) with health checks green for 7 days
milestones: 2026-02-10: Draft migration guide and SDK shim MVP
2026-02-24: Customer advance notice (60-day window) sent to active affected customers
2026-04-15: Broader migration enforcement begins (soft redirects and telemetry enforcement)
2026-05-15: Hard deprecation: remove tag routing and return explicit 410 for retired tags
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Significant customer usage on legacy tags discovered late. Mitigation: Extend soft-redirect window and offer concierge migration for top 20 customers.
Risk: SDK shim edge-case failures. Mitigation: Partner with Eng to add end-to-end tests against representative workloads and maintain a short-lived emergency rollback path.
Risk: Release notes/comm messaging misunderstood. Mitigation: Multi-channel comms (email, Console banner, in-product modal, account exec outreach) and a single FAQ doc.
Risk: Legal/compliance objections for private deployments. Mitigation: Engage Security & Legal in the 2-week review earlier and provide an on-prem compatibility patch schedule.
